hypotheses.justification: The conclusion is that `fun s => s.val i` is surjective. The proof begins by introducing `x : F.obj i`. If `F.obj i` is empty, surjectivity holds vacuously. Otherwise, the element `x` together with the other hypotheses makes every `F.obj j` nonempty. Take any `j`. Because `J` is `IsCofilteredOrEmpty`, the field `IsCofilteredOrEmpty.cone_objs i j` gives some `k` with morphisms `f : k ⟶ i` and `g : k ⟶ j`. By `Fsur f`, `x` has a preimage `y : F.obj k`, and then `F.map g y : F.obj j`. So at the start of the proof, after `fun x =>`, we can add `haveI : ∀ j, Nonempty (F.obj j) := fun j => by obtain ⟨k, f, g, -⟩ := IsCofilteredOrEmpty.cone_objs i j; exact ⟨F.map g (Fsur f x).choose⟩`. The rest of the proof is unchanged: this local instance is all that `toPreimages_nonempty_of_surjective` (and indirectly `nonempty_sections_of_finite_cofiltered_system`) need. So the instance argument can be dropped, for example with `omit [∀ j : J, Nonempty (F.obj j)] in`. The other hypotheses are needed: Finite (Kőnig's lemma), the cofilteredness (a parallel pair with maps id and swap on a 2-element set has no sections), and Fsur.
